info.title: ocrmd /api/v1
info.description: The API the ocrmd phone app speaks. Generated by tools/gen_reference.py from ocrmd/web/v1.py — do not edit by hand.

get.description: Open to anyone who can reach the port: says only that this is ocrmd and whether to pair.

post.description: Exchange a pairing code made on the computer (`ocrmd pair`) for this device's token.

get.description: The device this request's token belongs to.
What this server can do: API version, access mode, whether pages get the model's reading now, OCR engines.
Paired devices and pending codes. This computer only.

post.description:
A one-time code for a phone, with the link and QR code that carry it. The server URL is the LAN
address when `serve --lan` bound every interface.

delete.description: Revoke a device (or cancel a pending code) by id or name. This computer only.

get.description: Every document in the library, with its catalogue entry and progress.

post.description: Start a new document before its first capture, so it has a title from the first page on.

get.description: One document with a row (and a thumbnail) per page.
Full-text search over every page of every document (or of `doc`).
A page: its reconciled text, open disagreements, verdict, images and neighbours.

put.description: A human edit: it survives the next `verify`.

get.description: A picture of the page: `flat`, `processed`, `bin` or `raw`; `?max=` scales it down to a JPEG.

parameters.name: max

schema.description: long side in px; answers a JPEG
schema.title: Max

parameters.description: long side in px; answers a JPEG

post.description: Settle one disagreement with the OCR reading, the model's, or your own text.
Mark the page reviewed; refused (409) while a disagreement is open. The reviewer defaults to the device's name.

One photo from the phone's camera → a page (or two, for a spread), read twice like any other.

Answers at once with the ingest job; poll `GET /jobs/{id}` for `results`. Send a `client_id` and a
retry of the same photo returns the same job instead of a second one — and should the server have
restarted in between, the capture's own sha256 recognises it as a duplicate rather than a new page.
`origin` says whether the photo is the camera's frame (`camera`, cropped here like any capture) or
a page the phone's document scanner already cropped (`scanner`); the page's `source.type` keeps
the difference (`mobile` / `mobile_scan`), since a scanner's crop is not the raw frame.
Run the stages a document's pages are missing (the model pass for pages captured OCR-only).

get.description: Recent jobs, newest first; `active` keeps the queued and running ones.
A job's progress and, for a capture, what became of the photo (`results`).

CaptureResult.title: CaptureResult
CaptureResult.description: What became of one uploaded photo.

Flag.title: Flag
Flag.description: One open disagreement: `ocr` and `llm` are the two readings, `context` the text around the mark.

log.title: Log
log.description: the last lines of the job's log

images.title: Images
images.description: flat | processed | bin | raw → URL; add ?max=N for a smaller JPEG

name.title: Name
